newsitem.title: USA: Harman sees Chrysler affecting Q4 results.
newsitem.headline: Harman sees Chrysler affecting Q4 results.

text.p: Harman International Industries Inc said Wednesday that the duration of a strike at an auto plant would determine how well it would do in the fourth quarter.

"The Chrysler (Corp ) Mound Road plant, which supplies engines for the Jeep Grand Cherokee and the Dodge Ram and Dakota pickup trucks, has been on strike since April 10," it said. "The duration of the strike and the effect on Chrysler production releases will determine the impact on Harman's fourth quarter results."

The company, which makes high-fidelity audio products, said it otherwise expected "excellent" results in its 1997 fiscal fourth quarter and fiscal 1998, driven by new product introductions in the Consumer and Professional businesses and "success" in the original equipment manufacturer automotive business.
Harman reported third-quarter earnings of $0.56 a share against $0.86 for the same period last year. First Call's consensus among analysts projected $0.51 for the quarter.
For the fourth-quarter, the consensus foresees $1.05 a share against $0.97 a year ago.
On Monday, Chrysler officials met with union leaders representing more than 1,800 workers.
It was the first time that it had met with the United Auto Workers union since the strike erupted to protest against its decision to shift production of drive shafts to an outside supplier.
